“Margaret’s Waltz” ~ a curious transcription in 9/8

http://abcnotation.com/tunePage?a=homepages.ihug.co.nz/~dexy/music/celticl/0047

Margaret’s Waltz (Variation)
In the file celticl.abc from Dexter N. Muir

There was also a time problem with one of the bars and the B-part was repeated with a first and second ending, offering a variant on the last 8 bars.. I’ve removed the suggested chords, which I’ll add later. I’ve also re-transcribed this from 9/8 to 3/4, waltz time, and I’ve corrected the one bar that was too long, and removed the incorrect repetition of the B-part. Two turns on c (~c>A) have also been removed.

Margaret’s Waltz by P. Sh-Sh.

This was published by the English Folk Dance and Song Society in A major and also exists in an identical hand-written score, apparently done by Pat Shaw, (P. Sh-Sh), in a document which also describes the dance. It concludes with “This dance together with its tune is dedicated to Margaret Grant who has done so much in the South West Area to encourage Folk Dance Music and Song on the right lines. It was first performed at a Country Dance party from Clyst St. George on March 25th, 1959.”

X:7 is almost identical to that version, transposed to G. The only differences from that published version are that the B2 B2 in measure 7 was B4 and measure 18 was
|g3 f e2| rather than |g2 f2 e2|.
